residue.text: Eleven normal inspections plus B9 correction require all thirteen inspection minutes: any inspection idle time defeats the deadline. Blocked unloading occupies the transfer clerk; the inspector cannot assist transfer. No additional staff or capacity can rescue the window. Removing power can preserve output while increasing transfer burden.

The count signature identifies inspection work, but correcting B9 is already mandatory. Starting a hand trip after supply starvation is diagnosed may restore eligibility yet cannot undo inspection idle time. A consequential signature-conditioned transport action and advantage over the closest feasible rival remain unestablished; anomaly recognition alone does not establish an opening.

The discrepancy cause is unknown and implies no other defect. Later smaller, more frequent requests remain an unobserved hypothesis and do not change fixed demand. Schedules and sensor benefits are finite-model predictions, not trial results, empirical distributions or a global optimality proof.

summary.text: Require twelve correct sealed releases by boundary 13; rank transfer occupied minutes only among complete successes. Preserve five rack places, whole-load unloading, source and inspection order, uninterrupted operations and two trolley allowances. P1 concerns nine source carriers; P2 concerns all twelve.

Attack the account that timely release requires powered trolley service; timely eligible rack supply is the surviving function. Model hypothesis: consecutive hand trips starting at 0 deliver B4-B12 at boundaries 1-9, permitting continuous inspection through 13 with nine transfer minutes. Closest rival: trolley B4-B7 during 0-3, trolley B8-B11 during 3-6, then hand B12 during 6-7, predicts completion at 13 with seven transfer minutes.

Retain the observed failure signature: B9 has a ten-bracket mark but a count of nine. Proposed WHERE rule: that signature on the active carrier selects inspection correction, recount and sealing; an empty eligible queue with source carriers selects a permitted hand trip when the transfer clerk is free. Missing releases must not automatically be attributed to trolley failure.

Record boundary unload identities, rack eligibility, active counts and inspection duration, correct completed releases and both clerks occupied intervals. Supply-starvation predicts an empty eligible queue and idle inspector; B9 correction predicts count nine with an occupied surface for two minutes despite supply. Defeat the sensor claim if observations cannot separate these accounts or conditional control cannot outperform its closest feasible rival.
